title: Kharijites
capsule: The Kharijites emerged from the First Fitna as warriors who rejected both Ali ibn Abi Talib and Mu'awiya after the arbitration of Siffin (657 CE), holding that any Muslim could be caliph and that grave sinners forfeited their Muslim status. Ali crushed the main force at the Battle of Nahrawan in 658 CE, but Kharijite cells persisted and a Kharijite assassin killed Ali in 661. During the Umayyad period Kharijite insurrections erupted repeatedly across Iraq, Persia, and North Africa; the Ibadi branch, the most moderate faction, established enduring communities in Oman and North Africa, while the more radical Azraqite and Sufrite branches mounted major revolts suppressed by al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf between 695 and 697. The 751–763 window likely corresponds to a specific Kharijite political entity in the Maghreb or Iraq.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Kharijite political entities were fragmented and short-lived; mapping a single bounded territory to this entry is inherently uncertain, as the movement operated as dispersed insurrectionary cells across a wide area.
